thread:
scanner-bot: Image CI SBOM + vuln scan: HIGH CVE found in base image openssl@1.1.1k (CVE-2026-4002) used by redwood/runtime:2026-04-02-rc3
scanner-bot: SBOM note: package-lock != installed tree (drift) and image signature missing

mia (security): tagging @devon @alex @sana for triage

devon (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally. base: debian:bullseye + openssl 1.1.1k via /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.1.1

devon (eng-runtime): `docker run --rm -it redwood/runtime:2026-04-02-rc3 bash -c "ldd /usr/bin/our-service | grep ssl"`
devon (eng-runtime): Confirmed vulnerable binary present in prod RC image

alex (eng-platform): Important: the image was missing our standard cosign signature and SBOM hash mismatch. How did it get past CI? @sana any pipeline logs?

sana (eng-sre): Checking build pipeline... found manual push step by CI-maintainer bot at 2026-04-02T09:12Z that skipped SBOM validation due to `SKIP_SBOM=true` flag. Investigating who set the flag.

sana (eng-sre): Audit: push triggered by service-account: ci-bot@infra. Listing recent commits in runtime repo.

sre-bot: Activity log snippet:
```
2026-04-02T09:11:58Z ci-bot@infra pushed image redwood/runtime:2026-04-02-rc3
SBOM_check: skipped
signature: none
```

mia (security): Containment plan:
- Revoke current RC and block the image tag in registry
- Emergency rebuild with updated base (openssl patched to 1.1.1m) and normal SBOM+signing
- Rotate any KMS signing keys used by CI if they were exposed by missing signatures (audit first)
- Audit RBAC: who can set SKIP_SBOM flag in pipeline and restrict

paul (legal): If images were deployed to customer-facing infra we may need notification. Mia, pls assess exposure and whether keys/certs have been touched.

devon (eng-runtime): I'll prepare base update PR to use patched base: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/450
devon (eng-runtime): Also adding a blocker: `enforce_sbom && require_signature` in pipeline config

alex (eng-platform): Platform will add an enforcement rule in registry to reject unsigned images and add SBOM parity check. Also we'll add CI policy that disallows SKIP_SBOM unless 2 approvers

sana (eng-sre): RBAC action: creating infra-ops ticket to remove SKIP_SBOM capability from ci-bot service-account and require human approver for any bypass. Ticket: SRE-311

sre-bot: Rebuild finished. Staging image redwood/runtime:staging-2026-04-02-1 scanned: no HIGH CVEs. SBOM attached and cosign signature present (key_id=projects/redwood-kms/keys/imgsign1)

sana (eng-sre): Promoting canary to 5% traffic now. Will monitor for 30 minutes.

mia (security): Also initiating post-incident action items (SEC-PIPE-77):
- Lockdown SKIP_SBOM RBAC and document exceptions (owner: eng-sre)
- Add automated enforcement of cosign signatures in registry (owner: eng-platform)
- Add CI gate for SBOM vs installed tree parity (owner: eng-runtime)
- Run audit of images pushed in last 30 days for unsigned or mismatched SBOMs (owner: security)
- Update incident runbook to include KMS key rotation checklist (owner: security)

alex (eng-platform): Noted. Legal to be kept in loop if exposure found.

paul (legal): Thanks. Please ping if there's any PII or secrets in images.

devon (eng-runtime): Canary passed. Promoting signed image redwood/runtime:2026-04-02-1 to prod after 1 hour of stable metrics

auth-bot: Registry denylist applied: redwood/runtime:2026-04-02-rc3 -> blocked

mia (security): Closing thread after retro. Will schedule 45-min postmortem tomorrow. :lock:

scanner-bot: Monitoring continues; will reopen if new anomalies detected.
